blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a LinkedIn paper from KDD'18 that introduces an automated system for optimizing the ranking of items in a user's feed. Previously, LinkedIn relied on manual tuning of feature weights, which was time-consuming and required repeated effort with every significant change. The new approach eliminates this manual process, significantly boosting developer productivity while achieving better Pareto optimal solutions. The system uses multi-objective optimization to balance competing metrics like Viral Actions (VA), Engaged Feed Sessions (EFS), and Job Applies (JA), with VA as the primary metric. The key insight is the application of a modified Thompson sampling algorithm to automate parameter selection, which avoids local optima through a combination of posterior sampling and uniform exploration. The system is deployed in production at LinkedIn, delivering substantial metric gains and improved performance.
paper_title: Online parameter selection for web-based ranking problems
